currency.basis: The bank's present homepage displays the SVG beside its new MyRaif app banner. This is current first-party presentation, not a historical attribution of the base.

identity.basis: The official name-change announcement and current Ukrainian website tie the current Raiffeisen Bank and its MyRaif graphic to the bank formerly known as Raiffeisen Bank Aval in the record.

assessment.independenceRationale: These are first-party observations from the same bank, not independent sources; the bank's own identity announcement and current first-party usage are direct evidence.
uncertainties: Exact attribution of the accepted outlined variant is not established; this does not undermine the official candidate.

variant.basis: The official asset is a standalone, wordless mark with a separable yellow uniform field around the complete emblem. The unboxed emblem is also present in the current header. It is suitable for a square cell; actual catalog circular adaptation and final fit remain to be verified.

candidate.detailsJudgement: Full original librsvg source and exact Compose Desktop source/final comparisons show the same complete dark crossed-horse emblem, including notches, negative space, proportions and color. Only its background silhouette changes; no tracing, cropping or internal recoloring. No clipping observed.
candidate.proportionsJudgement: The source has a separable uniform yellow field and centered complete emblem away from its edges: plain-field type 1. The equal-color circular backing preserves original emblem position and scale, leaving visible clearances. Resized 24, 32 and 48 px diagnostics from bound Desktop frames remain recognizable in both themes; these are not native mobile checks.
candidate.rationale: Current official MyRaif vector supplies the standalone Ukrainian bank mark without the enclosing square of the accepted icon. Its larger, unboxed crossed-horse emblem is visibly different and consistent with the current official bank presentation. Baseline attribution is unknown, so this is a supported replacement rather than a claimed dated rebrand.
transforms: Separated the uniform yellow background from the complete centered emblem and replaced its rounded square with a same-color #FFED00 circle; transparency remains outside. Kept the original #231F20 emblem path, position and scale unchanged.

candidate.variant: Original official dark crossed-horse emblem on an adapted yellow catalog circle; not a claim that a circular official avatar was observed.
candidate.visibleDiffExplanation: Both desktop before/after views show the black square border removed, the crossed-horse emblem larger and differently shaped, and a more saturated yellow field. The source directly supports the new unboxed version; this does not prove the old symbol's origin or a precise transition date.

proposals.reason: The official Ukrainian bank's current MyRaif app graphic presents the crossed-horse-head mark without the black enclosing square present in the accepted icon. Its official vector is a suitable standalone mark; the different frame and emblem geometry justify a source-supported update, not merely reserialization. The exact attribution and current use of the old square-outline icon remain unconfirmed.

sourceCandidate.rationale: The original vector is the official current bank MyRaif app graphic: a clear standalone symbol with no separate lettering. Its unboxed mark and geometry differ visibly from the outlined accepted icon. Use the permitted same-color circular catalog backing after verifying whole-emblem fit and source fidelity.

sources.observation: The Ukrainian bank's current homepage displays this SVG beside its New MyRaif app banner. The downloaded first-party SVG is a dark standalone crossed-horse-head symbol on yellow rounded-square background, formed from paths without raster. The homepage identifies Raiffeisen Bank in Ukraine.
In its 17 June 2021 announcement the bank said Raiffeisen Bank Aval Joint Stock Company officially changed its name to Raiffeisen Bank Joint Stock Company and continues obligations as successor.
The current homepage header uses a full logo with a similar unboxed crossed-horse-head mark beside the name and slogan; the full lockup is not the replacement icon.
